items.question: In the AW139 RFM, 'safe OEI flight' is generally defined as:
options: A sustainable airspeed of at least 50 KIAS, a positive rate of climb at acceptable power, and enough altitude to manoeuvre clear of terrain and obstacles.
Any airspeed above Vmini, a level flight path, and gear down.
The ability to maintain hover OGE on one engine at any convenient airspeed.
Climb at VYSE with both engines running and altitude sufficient to reach destination.
items.explanation: Safe OEI flight combines a minimum airspeed, a positive climb at acceptable power, and altitude that allows manoeuvring clear of terrain and obstacles.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: SAFE OEI FLIGHT (p.3-1)

items.question: Which minimum airspeed is part of the AW139 'safe OEI flight' definition?
options: 40 KIAS
50 KIAS
60 KIAS
70 KIAS
items.explanation: The RFM defines safe OEI flight as including a sustainable airspeed of not less than 50 KIAS.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: SAFE OEI FLIGHT (p.3-1)

items.question: According to the AW139 emergency landing guidance, what does 'Land immediately' mean?
options: Land at once, even if this means ditching or landing in trees at a normally unsuitable site.
Land at the nearest airfield where assistance is available.
Land at the next scheduled destination.
Continue flight until fuel allows a convenient landing.
items.explanation: 'Land immediately' means landing at once, even at a site that would normally be considered unsuitable, because continued flight is more hazardous.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: EMERGENCY LANDING GUIDANCE (p.3-2)

items.question: According to the AW139 emergency landing guidance, 'Land as soon as possible' means you should:
options: Land at once, regardless of surface suitability.
Not continue flight longer than necessary to achieve a safe and unhurried landing at the nearest site.
Continue flight to the destination if weather permits.
Land only when a maintenance engineer is available.
items.explanation: 'Land as soon as possible' directs the crew to terminate the flight without delay at the nearest site where a safe, unhurried landing can be made.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: EMERGENCY LANDING GUIDANCE (p.3-2)

items.question: According to the AW139 emergency landing guidance, 'Land as soon as practicable' means:
options: Land immediately at the closest point on the ground.
Land only if the situation worsens.
Land at the nearest aviation location or safe landing site selected for subsequent convenience.
Continue flight to planned destination without restriction.
items.explanation: 'Land as soon as practicable' allows the crew to proceed to the nearest aviation location or other safe site chosen with later assistance and convenience in mind.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: EMERGENCY LANDING GUIDANCE (p.3-2)

items.question: When a procedure in the AW139 RFM concludes with 'Land as soon as possible', how should the pilot interpret this?
options: Flight may be continued to destination without time pressure.
Land at once, even if it requires landing in trees or water.
Do not continue flight longer than needed to reach the nearest site where a safe, unhurried landing can be made.
Continue flight until a maintenance base is reached.
items.explanation: 'Land as soon as possible' means the flight should only continue as long as required to reach the nearest site where a safe, unhurried landing can be made.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: EMERGENCY LANDING GUIDANCE (p.3-2)

items.question: In the AW139, what is stated as the prime consideration immediately after partial or complete power failure?
options: Start timing for a Mayday call.
Establish a safe flight condition before analysing the cause of the failure.
Immediately attempt an in-flight engine restart.
Reduce airspeed to below Vmini to minimise sink rate.
items.explanation: The RFM emphasises that establishing a safe flight condition is the prime consideration before analysing the cause of the failure.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: ENGINE FAILURE (p.3-16)

items.question: Which set of cues best matches the AW139 'ENGINE FAILURE RECOGNITION' description?
options: Noticeable right sideslip, ENG OUT CAS warning, 'ENGINE 1(2) OUT' voice, torque split between engines, and possible NR drop.
Noticeable left sideslip, MGB CHIP warning, loud bang from main gearbox, and immediate NR increase.
No yaw change, HYD SYS 1 and 2 cautions, AFCS OFF, and stable torque on both engines.
Sudden roll to the left, FUEL FILT BYPASS message, and stabilised NR at 110%.
items.explanation: Engine failure cues include right sideslip (nose left), ENG OUT CAS warning, 'ENGINE 1(2) OUT' voice, significant torque split, and possibly a drop in NR.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: ENGINE FAILURE RECOGNITION (p.3-16)

items.question: Following a single engine failure in the AW139, what happens to the operating engine and rotor speed?
options: Torque on the live engine decreases and NR always increases.
Torque on the live engine increases and NR may drop, requiring collective adjustment.
Torque on the live engine remains unchanged while NR freezes at 100%.
Both torque and NR instantly drop to idle values.
items.explanation: A single engine failure results in increased torque on the live engine and may cause an NR drop that must be controlled with collective.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE (p.3-16)

items.question: After executing the ENGINE FAILURE procedure, when should an engine restart in flight be considered in the AW139?
options: Immediately, before any other checklist items.
Only after the cause of the failure has been analysed and is believed corrected.
Never; restart in flight is prohibited in the AW139.
Only when flying over water or mountainous terrain.
items.explanation: The RFM states that an in-flight restart should only be considered after the cause of the failure has been analysed and corrected.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE (p.3-16)

items.question: In a SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE IN HOVER (5 to 10 ft), what is the initial collective pitch action according to the AW139 RFM?
options: Lower collective rapidly to minimum and allow a hard touchdown.
Maintain collective or lower it slightly if required to establish descent.
Raise collective to maintain hover height until power is recovered.
Retard ENG MODE switches to IDLE before changing collective.
items.explanation: The procedure calls for maintaining collective or lowering it slightly to establish a controlled descent from a low hover.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE IN HOVER (p.3-17)

items.question: During a SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE IN HOVER (5 to 10 ft), how should collective be used as touchdown becomes imminent?
options: Leave collective unchanged and allow the aircraft to settle.
Increase collective to cushion the landing.
Lower collective fully to minimise bounce.
Cycle collective up and down to dissipate energy.
items.explanation: As touchdown becomes imminent, collective is increased to cushion the landing.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE IN HOVER (p.3-17)

items.question: After touchdown following a SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE IN HOVER, what is the prescribed control action?
options: Hold cyclic aft and increase collective to keep weight off the gear.
Centralise cyclic and simultaneously reduce collective to minimum, using wheel brakes as required.
Apply full left cyclic and maintain collective to avoid roll-over.
Release all controls and let the aircraft coast to a stop.
items.explanation: After touchdown the cyclic is centralised and collective reduced to minimum, with wheel brakes applied as required.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE IN HOVER (p.3-17)

items.question: For a rejected take-off after SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE ON TAKE OFF CATEGORY B, what is the first collective action?
options: Increase collective to reduce rate of descent.
Reduce collective as necessary to maintain rotor RPM if altitude permits.
Hold collective fixed and use cyclic only.
Lower collective fully to ground-idle pitch.
items.explanation: The rejected take-off procedure calls for reducing collective as necessary to maintain rotor RPM, provided altitude permits.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE ON TAKE OFF CATEGORY B (p.3-17)

items.question: During a rejected SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE ON TAKE OFF CATEGORY B, what is the maximum flare angle close to the ground?
items.explanation: The RFM limits the flare during a rejected take-off to 15° when close to the ground.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE ON TAKE OFF CATEGORY B (p.3-17)

items.question: In a SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE DURING CRUISE, how is safe OEI flight established according to the AW139 RFM?
options: Use cyclic to establish safe OEI flight while collective is adjusted to maintain rotor RPM and torque within limits.
Lower collective to minimum and use pedals only.
Raise collective to maximum continuous power before adjusting cyclic.
Trim for minimum speed and ignore torque indications.
items.explanation: The procedure calls for adjusting collective to keep NR and torque within limits, then using cyclic to establish safe OEI flight.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: SINGLE ENGINE FAILURE DURING CRUISE (p.3-18)

items.question: What does the AW139 RFM state about a sequential or simultaneous failure of both engines?
options: It can be handled as a normal OEI climb.
It requires immediate entry into autorotation.
It requires landing gear retraction and acceleration to Vne.
It can be ignored if NR remains within limits.
items.explanation: The RFM states that a sequential or simultaneous failure of both engines will require entry into autorotation.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: DOUBLE ENGINE FAILURE (p.3-20)

items.question: With a simultaneous failure of both engines, what happens to rotor speed (NR) and what is required from the pilot?
options: NR increases rapidly, requiring immediate collective increase.
NR remains constant; no collective adjustment is needed.
NR drops rapidly, requiring a large and rapid collective reduction to recover NR into the Power Off range.
NR slowly decreases and should be allowed to stabilise without control input.
items.explanation: A simultaneous failure of both engines produces a rapid NR drop that must be countered by a large and rapid collective reduction to keep NR in the Power Off range.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: ENTRY IN AUTOROTATION (p.3-20)

items.question: Assuming an average autorotative sink rate of about 2500 ft/min, what minimum AGL height does the AW139 RFM state is required to provide enough time to complete a double-engine restart?
items.explanation: At an autorotative sink rate of about 2500 ft/min, the RFM notes that roughly 3000–4000 ft AGL are required to give sufficient time to complete the restart procedures.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: DOUBLE ENGINE FAILURE (p.3-20)

items.question: During the AW139 autorotative landing procedure, which airspeed range is recommended in autorotation?
options: 60–80 KIAS (best range to minimum sink)
70–90 KIAS (hover-taxi range)
80–100 KIAS (minimum rate of descent to best range speed)
90–110 KIAS (Vne to Vno range)
items.explanation: The autorotation procedure calls for 80 KIAS as minimum rate of descent speed and 100 KIAS as best range speed.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: AUTOROTATIVE LANDING PROCEDURE ON LAND (p.3-21)

items.question: In the AW139 autorotative landing procedure, to what rotor speed (NR) may collective be adjusted during autorotation?
options: Up to 100% NR
Up to 105% NR
Up to 110% NR
Up to 115% NR
items.explanation: The procedure specifies adjusting collective to obtain up to 110% NR in autorotation.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: AUTOROTATIVE LANDING PROCEDURE ON LAND (p.3-21)

items.question: Approximately at what height AGL should the cyclic flare be initiated during an autorotative landing according to the AW139 RFM?
options: 100 ft AGL
150 ft AGL
200 ft AGL
300 ft AGL
items.explanation: The autorotative landing procedure calls for initiating the flare at approximately 200 ft AGL.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: AUTOROTATIVE LANDING PROCEDURE ON LAND (p.3-21)

items.question: What is the maximum nose-up attitude during the flare in the AW139 autorotative landing procedure?
items.explanation: The RFM limits the flare attitude to a maximum of about 30° nose up.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: AUTOROTATIVE LANDING PROCEDURE ON LAND (p.3-21)

items.question: Which set of cues is described for a TAIL ROTOR DRIVE FAILURE in the AW139?
options: Aircraft yaws rapidly to the right, pedals lose effectiveness, and there may be noise and vibration from the aft fuselage.
Aircraft yaws rapidly to the left with strong nose-down pitch.
No yaw change, but a loud bang from the main gearbox and severe vertical vibration.
Loss of all hydraulic pressure and AFCS OFF.
items.explanation: Tail rotor drive failure cues include rapid yaw to the right, loss of yaw control with ineffective pedals, and possible noise/vibration from the aft fuselage area.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: TAIL ROTOR DRIVE FAILURE (p.3-44)

items.question: In a TAIL ROTOR DRIVE FAILURE in hover, what is the immediate collective action?
options: Raise collective to arrest yaw and stay in the hover.
Lower collective to LAND IMMEDIATELY while maintaining attitude and minimising lateral translation with cyclic.
Leave collective unchanged and use pedals only.
Lower collective to minimum and then raise it to full.
items.explanation: In hover, the procedure calls for lowering collective to land immediately while maintaining attitude and minimising lateral translation.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: TAIL ROTOR DRIVE FAILURE (p.3-44)

items.question: In forward flight with a TAIL ROTOR DRIVE FAILURE, what is the first action on collective according to the AW139 RFM?
options: Raise collective to reduce yaw rate.
Lower collective immediately to minimise yaw to the right.
Set collective to maximum continuous and hold.
Do not touch collective; use cyclic only.
items.explanation: In forward flight, collective is lowered immediately to minimise yaw to the right and help regain control.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: TAIL ROTOR DRIVE FAILURE (p.3-44)

items.question: In tail rotor failure procedures, how can collective be used to help control sideslip while maintaining NR within limits?
options: Increasing collective tends to yaw the nose to the right.
Raising or lowering collective can help control sideslip; increasing collective tends to yaw the nose to the left.
Collective has no effect on yaw in tail rotor failures.
Lowering collective always yaws the nose left, regardless of configuration.
items.explanation: The note emphasises that raising or lowering collective while keeping NR within limits can help control sideslip, with increased collective tending to yaw the nose left.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: TAIL ROTOR DRIVE FAILURE (p.3-44)

items.question: In a TAIL ROTOR CONTROL SYSTEM FAILURE, what happens to the tail rotor blade pitch according to the AW139 RFM?
options: Blades drive to full right thrust.
Blades drive to full left thrust.
Blades float to a pitch angle of approximately zero thrust, depending on flight condition.
Blades feather to minimise drag but maintain full thrust.
items.explanation: A control system failure causes the tail rotor blades to 'float' to a pitch angle of approximately zero thrust, depending on flight condition.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: TAIL ROTOR CONTROL SYSTEM FAILURE (p.3-45)

items.question: Which cues are listed for a TAIL ROTOR CONTROL SYSTEM FAILURE in the AW139?
options: Aircraft yaws left or right and pedals are free but ineffective or only partially effective.
No yaw change, but collective becomes jammed.
Sudden roll with AFCS OFF and HYD SYS 2 caution.
ENG OUT warning only.
items.explanation: The RFM notes that the aircraft may yaw left or right and that pedals may be free but ineffective or only partially effective.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: TAIL ROTOR CONTROL SYSTEM FAILURE (p.3-45)

items.question: In low hover with a TAIL ROTOR CONTROL SYSTEM FAILURE, what is the prescribed immediate action?
options: Raise collective to maintain hover and diagnose the failure.
Lower collective to LAND IMMEDIATELY while maintaining attitude and minimising lateral translation.
Leave collective fixed and use pedals only.
Retard ENG MODE switches to IDLE before changing collective.
items.explanation: In low hover, the procedure calls for lowering collective to land immediately while maintaining attitude and minimising lateral translation.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: TAIL ROTOR CONTROL SYSTEM FAILURE (p.3-45)

items.question: In forward flight or high hover with a TAIL ROTOR CONTROL SYSTEM FAILURE, what is the initial handling guidance?
options: Select autopilot OFF and descend straight ahead at any speed.
Attempt to determine a combination of speed and power that minimises yaw and then carefully assess pedal effectiveness.
Lower collective to minimum and allow yaw to stabilise without changing speed.
Raise collective to maximum OEI power and ignore yaw.
items.explanation: The procedure calls for establishing a speed/power combination that minimises yaw, then carefully assessing pedal response to diagnose the failure.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: TAIL ROTOR CONTROL SYSTEM FAILURE (p.3-45)

items.question: In an ENGINE BAY FIRE (FLIGHT), once the fire warning has cleared after use of the fire extinguisher, what landing urgency does the AW139 RFM specify?
options: Continue flight to destination.
Land as soon as possible.
Land at the next maintenance base only.
Land as soon as practicable.
items.explanation: After the engine fire warning has cleared following extinguisher use, the RFM directs the crew to land as soon as possible.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: ENGINE BAY FIRE (FLIGHT) (p.3-26)

items.question: In an ENGINE BAY FIRE (FLIGHT) where the fire warning persists after extinguisher use, what landing urgency is emphasised?
options: Land immediately.
Land as soon as practicable.
Continue flight while monitoring.
Land at the nearest airfield when convenient.
items.explanation: Persistent engine bay fire indications call for the highest urgency; the RFM emphasises LAND IMMEDIATELY.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: ENGINE BAY FIRE (FLIGHT) (p.3-26–3-27)

items.question: In a BAGGAGE BAY FIRE, if smoke is present in the cabin, which landing recommendation is given?
options: Continue flight; the situation is not critical.
Land as soon as practicable.
Land as soon as possible.
Land immediately, even at an unsuitable site.
items.explanation: With smoke in the cabin from a baggage bay fire, the procedure instructs the crew to land as soon as possible.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: BAGGAGE BAY FIRE (p.3-27–3-28)

items.question: Following a BAGGAGE BAY FIRE indication in flight on the AW139, the baggage bay extinguisher has been discharged and the warning light goes out with no further signs of fire. Which statement best reflects the recommended landing strategy?
options: Continue the flight to destination as planned, since the indication is out.
Land immediately at the nearest suitable area regardless of conditions.
Land as soon as practicable, considering that the fire appears to be extinguished but the system is no longer available.
Climb to a higher altitude and monitor for at least 30 minutes before deciding to land.
items.explanation: After discharge and apparent extinguishing of a baggage bay fire, the guidance is generally to land as soon as practicable, as the extinguisher has been used and monitoring is still required.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: BAGGAGE BAY FIRE (p.3-27–3-28)

items.question: In case of a single HYDRAULIC SYSTEM 1 failure in flight, what is the primary pilot consideration according to the AW139 RFM?
options: Immediate landing is mandatory regardless of system redundancy.
Maintain control, avoid abrupt manoeuvres, and plan a landing as soon as practicable.
Disengage both autopilots and continue the flight to destination without restrictions.
Switch off all electrical systems to reduce hydraulic load.
items.explanation: For a single hydraulic system failure, the helicopter remains controllable but the RFM emphasises avoiding abrupt manoeuvres and planning a landing as soon as practicable.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: HYD SYS 1(2) FAILURE

items.question: Following a HYD SYS 2 failure in flight, how should the AW139 landing normally be planned?
options: Continue the flight to destination if weather is good.
Plan a landing as soon as practicable, preferably at an airfield or helipad with maintenance support.
Perform an immediate landing in the nearest field regardless of surface.
Land only after both hydraulic systems have failed.
items.explanation: A single HYD SYS failure calls for a landing as soon as practicable, preferably where maintenance is available, as described in the RFM.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: HYD SYS 1(2) FAILURE

items.question: What is the main risk highlighted in the AW139 RFM with a total loss of hydraulic power (HYD SYS 1 and 2) in flight?
options: Loss of AFCS only, with normal manual control.
Reduced engine performance but full control authority.
Significantly increased control forces and possible loss of controllability if speed and manoeuvres are not restricted.
Immediate engine flameout due to hydraulic pump seizure.
items.explanation: Total loss of hydraulics results in very high control forces and potential loss of controllability; the RFM stresses speed and manoeuvre limitations in this condition.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: HYD SYS 1+2 FAILURE

items.question: In case of a MAIN GENERATOR failure in flight on the AW139, what is the initial pilot action according to the electrical emergency procedures?
options: Switch both generators OFF immediately.
Check the associated GEN pushbutton and attempt reset in accordance with the checklist.
Pull all non-essential circuit breakers.
Select both engine control levers to IDLE.
items.explanation: The electrical failure procedure calls for verifying the affected generator pushbutton and attempting a reset as the first step, before further load shedding or landing decisions.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: MAIN GENERATOR FAILURE

items.question: Following a DUAL GENERATOR failure in flight, which of the following best describes the landing recommendation?
options: Continue the flight to destination using battery power only.
Land as soon as possible, giving priority to an area where a safe landing can be completed before essential power is depleted.
Descend to minimum safe altitude and hold until batteries are exhausted.
Climb to increase VHF communication range before considering any landing.
items.explanation: With both generators failed, the RFM calls for landing as soon as possible, considering remaining battery power and essential loads.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: DUAL GEN FAILURE

items.question: In the event of an ELECTRICAL FIRE or SMOKE in the cockpit, which initial crew action is highlighted in the AW139 RFM?
options: Open cabin doors immediately to vent smoke, regardless of airspeed.
Switch off all cockpit lighting and continue the flight.
Don oxygen masks (if installed), establish crew communication, and start isolating suspected electrical sources as per checklist.
Descend below 500 ft AGL and continue the flight visually.
items.explanation: The procedure for cockpit electrical fire/smoke emphasises crew protection (oxygen/smoke masks), establishing communication, and then isolating suspected electrical sources.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: ELECTRICAL FIRE/SMOKE

items.question: After a CABIN FIRE is reported in flight, what is the recommended priority according to the AW139 emergency procedures?
options: Extinguish the fire if possible, then land as soon as possible.
Continue flight at reduced power until smoke dissipates.
Open the baggage bay to ventilate the cabin.
Switch off both engines immediately without regard to flight path.
items.explanation: The cabin fire procedure directs the crew to fight the fire if practicable and then land as soon as possible to ensure occupant safety.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: CABIN FIRE

items.question: If an ENGINE BAY FIRE occurs in flight and the FIRE warning remains on after the first extinguisher bottle has been discharged, what does the AW139 RFM prescribe?
options: Ignore the indication if there is no visible smoke.
Discharge the second bottle and land immediately.
Continue the flight and rely on the baggage bay extinguisher.
Reset the fire detection system and monitor.
items.explanation: Persisting engine bay fire indications require discharge of the second bottle and an immediate landing, as per the engine bay fire checklist.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: ENGINE BAY FIRE (FLIGHT)

items.question: In case of MGB OIL PRESS LOW indication in flight, what is the primary landing recommendation in the AW139 RFM?
options: Continue to destination while monitoring temperature only.
Land as soon as possible, considering the potential for gearbox failure.
Descend to sea level and continue flight at reduced power.
Climb to a higher altitude to reduce gearbox load.
items.explanation: Low main gearbox oil pressure is treated as a serious condition, with the RFM calling for landing as soon as possible.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: MGB OIL PRESS LOW

items.question: When a MGB OIL TEMP HIGH warning is received without associated pressure loss, what does the AW139 RFM generally recommend?
options: Continue flight at any power setting.
Reduce power as much as practicable and land as soon as practicable.
Shut down both engines immediately.
Ignore the indication; it has no operational consequence.
items.explanation: High gearbox oil temperature without pressure loss still warrants reducing power and planning a landing as soon as practicable.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: MGB OIL TEMP HIGH

items.question: After a TRGB CHIP warning is triggered in flight, how should the landing be planned according to AW139 emergency procedures?
options: Continue normal operations; chip warnings are advisory only.
Land as soon as practicable, avoiding high-power manoeuvres.
Descend to minimum safe altitude and hold until the chip light goes out.
Land only if a second chip warning is received.
items.explanation: A single tail rotor gearbox chip indication leads to a landing as soon as practicable while avoiding unnecessary high-power manoeuvres.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: TRGB CHIP

items.question: In the event of a MAIN ROTOR VIBRATION of unknown origin that is judged severe, what landing guidance does the AW139 RFM give?
options: Continue flight and monitor only.
Reduce speed to VNE and continue to destination.
Land as soon as possible at the nearest suitable site.
Climb to reduce vibration, then continue flight.
items.explanation: Severe main rotor vibration of unknown cause requires landing as soon as possible at the nearest suitable area.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: MAIN ROTOR VIBRATION

items.question: If the AW139 experiences UNCOMMANDED YAW in forward flight suspected to be related to tail rotor malfunction, what is one of the immediate pilot actions?
options: Increase collective rapidly to regain yaw control.
Reduce power and adjust airspeed to a value giving best directional controllability, preparing for a run-on landing.
Switch off the hydraulic systems to free the pedals.
Enter autorotation immediately regardless of height.
items.explanation: For suspected tail rotor issues in forward flight, the RFM calls for reducing power, adjusting airspeed for yaw control, and preparing for a run-on landing.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: UNCOMMANDED YAW / TAIL ROTOR MALFUNCTION

items.question: In case of an AFCS malfunction resulting in uncommanded pitch or roll attitude changes, what does the AW139 emergency procedure require first?
options: Pull both AFCS circuit breakers only.
Immediately select both APs OFF and transfer to manual control.
Reduce airspeed below 40 KIAS and engage HOV mode.
Switch off hydraulic system 1.
items.explanation: The AFCS malfunction procedure instructs the crew to disconnect the autopilots and assume manual control as the first step before further diagnosis.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: AFCS MALFUNCTION

items.question: When ICE ACCRETION is encountered in flight and anti-ice systems are unable to control ice build-up, what landing guidance is given in the AW139 RFM?
options: Climb above the icing layer and continue flight.
Descend below the icing layer and continue as planned.
Leave the icing conditions as soon as possible and land as soon as practicable at a suitable site.
Remain in the icing area at reduced speed until de-icing is effective.
items.explanation: If ice accretion cannot be controlled, the RFM tells the crew to exit the icing conditions and plan a landing as soon as practicable.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: FLIGHT IN ICING CONDITIONS

items.question: If a DOOR or WINDOW caution appears in flight indicating a door not properly closed, what is the typical recommendation?
options: Continue flight without limitation.
Reduce speed in accordance with door-open limitations and land as soon as practicable.
Increase speed to close the door aerodynamically.
Open all doors to equalise pressure.
items.explanation: Door or window cautions are normally handled by reducing speed to the appropriate limitation and planning a landing as soon as practicable to secure the door.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: DOOR NOT PROPERLY CLOSED

items.question: In the event of an ENGINE OIL PRESS LOW warning on one engine, what does the AW139 RFM generally prescribe?
options: Ignore the indication if torque is below 50 %.
Shut down the affected engine in accordance with the checklist and plan for single engine operation.
Shut down both engines immediately.
Continue flight as normal but avoid take-off power.
items.explanation: Low engine oil pressure on one engine usually requires shutting down that engine following the procedure and continuing as OEI where possible.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: ENGINE OIL PRESS LOW

items.question: If both engines flame out due to fuel exhaustion and a successful autorotative landing is performed, what post-landing action is emphasised in the AW139 RFM?
options: Attempt an immediate restart before rotor stops.
Remain seated with rotors turning for at least 10 minutes.
Shut down all remaining systems, secure the helicopter, and organise evacuation as necessary.
Taxi to the nearest fuel pump using battery power only.
items.explanation: After a double engine failure and autorotative landing, procedures focus on securing systems and helicopter and managing evacuation.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: DOUBLE ENGINE FAILURE / AUTOROTATIVE LANDING

items.question: When an emergency landing on water is inevitable and flotation gear (if installed) has been armed and deployed, what is one of the pilot considerations highlighted in the AW139 RFM?
options: Touch down at the highest possible forward speed to minimise sink rate.
Aim for a level attitude and minimum forward speed compatible with control, avoiding large pitch or roll rates at water contact.
Land with a steep nose-down attitude to slice into the water.
Maintain hover over the water and shut both engines down before descent.
items.explanation: Ditching guidance calls for a level attitude and minimum forward speed compatible with control, with low pitch/roll rates at contact.
references: AW139 RFM Sec 3: DITCHING / EMERGENCY LANDING ON WATER
